preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the mint() function with your address as recipient and any arbitrary amount. This will create new tokens out of thin air and deposit them into your account, causing token inflation and devaluing existing holders' tokens.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The KLingToken contract has a mint() function protected by onlyOwner modifier. The owner can arbitrarily mint tokens to any address, causing inflation and devaluing existing tokens. This is a classic owner privilege abuse vulnerability.
attempts.attack_strategy: Become the contract owner by overwriting the ownership storage slot, then call mint() to mint a large amount of tokens to our address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite the owner storage slot at position 0 with our address. 2. Call the mint() function with our address as recipient and a large amount. 3. Verify our token balance increased significantly.

attempts.feedback: 遭遇权限锁。请检查是否需要 `vm.prank` 伪造身份。原因: Ownable: caller is not the owner

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The mint() function requires the caller to be the owner. We need to either become the owner or impersonate the current owner.
attempts.attack_strategy: Read the current owner address by calling the owner() function, then use vm.prank() to impersonate that owner when calling mint().
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Call owner() on the contract to get the current owner address. 2. Use vm.prank() to impersonate the owner. 3. Call mint() to mint tokens to our address. 4. Verify balance increased.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because we assumed the owner storage slot was at position 0, but due to inheritance and storage layout, it might be at a different slot. Instead of trying to calculate the correct slot, we should read the current owner and impersonate them.
